prompt.brief: Design a CI/CD platform that turns source changes into tested, signed artifacts and safely deploys them across environments with approvals, rollback, and auditable provenance.
successSignals: Separate immutable source revisions and signed artifacts from mutable run state, environment configuration, and deployment status.
Use queue-backed isolated workers with cacheable build inputs, concurrency limits, and per-repository fairness.
Require test, security, provenance, and approval gates before promotion, with an atomic environment release pointer.
Explain secrets isolation, untrusted pull-request execution, retries, rollback, artifact retention, and audit trails.

functional: Register repositories and pipeline definitions, trigger runs, schedule build and test stages, and store logs and artifacts.
Promote signed artifacts through environments with approvals, progressive rollout, health checks, rollback, and release history.
Expose run status, stage logs, cache hits, test results, security findings, deployment events, and cancellation.
nonFunctional: Meet queue acknowledgement <=1s under normal load.
Scale to 100K pipeline runs per day with bursty repositories without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100K pipeline runs per day with bursty repositories
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

dataFlow.title: Accept run a pipeline from a source change
dataFlow.description: The CI/CD platform gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The control plane records a versioned pipeline run, commit identity, and idempotency key before scheduling work.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed CI/CD platform events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.title: Build the read model
dataFlow.description: Partitioned workers consume CI/CD platform events, update the serving projection, and expose lag or watermark metadata.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the CI/CD platform projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

architecture.title: Build, test, artifact, approval, and deployment orchestration reference architecture
architecture.summary: The authoritative state records run a pipeline from a source change; asynchronous workers build serving projections while workers, artifact storage, deployment, and notifications stays isolated from the request path.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the CI/CD platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional CI/CD platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return CI/CD platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition CI/CD platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound CI/CD platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for CI/CD platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable CI/CD platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable CI/CD platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure CI/CD platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines source-triggered builds, gates, artifacts, deployment, scale, durability, and failure contracts.
Entities and commit/run/environment keys support build, test, approvals, deployment, security, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain CI/CD platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
